about: 2026-11-23 ljrole (ROUND 7, the lumberjacks a role of the game's computer player): lumberjack_twitch over FIVE matches, without the per-step trace -- the user's twelve (qa_lj_set 1), player 1 at his controller (qa_lj_p1 3), the walk-out probe every 30 s. Every phase within its jitter limit at every match's end. 2026-11-23 ljtwitch: the twitching check, as the user played it -- Steve Austin (player 1 at his controller, qa_lj_p1 3: after his opponent, out by himself now and then) against Kurt Angle, with the twelve lumberjacks of the user's 11-23 match (qa_lj_set 1: Savage, D-Lo Brown, La Parka, Brickowski, Taka Michinoku, British Bulldog, Shane McMahon, Han Zo Mon, Raven, Sting, X-Pac, Dean Malenko -- ten imported men), three matches. The user: 'There's still some twitching' / 'Its not just when they're at posts' / 'Check when they're idle outside the ring, thats where I notice most'. The jitter measure (lumberjack.c qa_jitter: every man every step -- turns reversed within 1/3 s of any size, animation files switched back within 2/3 s or restarted, states switched back, steps reversed) by what each man is doing: lj_p idle outside the ring (at the post or anywhere on the floor in no job), lj_q walking (the intro too), lj_r on a man / brawling / busy, lj_s the competitors out. The per-step trace (qa_lj_trace 4) is in the game's log for the analysis (scratch jit.py). ljround8 (2026-11-23): the aggression (hits a minute out on each competitor, the CPU as much as the player), the holds' throw / grapple-move split, the escape loop (0) and the intro's stops (0) checked.

ljtwitch: the lumberjacks IDLE outside the ring stand still -- at their posts, anywhere else on the floor in no job, or walking back to their posts (the user, 11-23: 'There's still some twitching' / 'Check when they're idle outside the ring, thats where I notice most'): at most one jitter event a 5 lumberjack-seconds -- a turn reversed within 1/3 s (both turns 3 of 4096 or more), the walk / stand files switched back within 2/3 s, a step reversing the last one's way. Before the fix (937b34d): 6 to 11 a lumberjack-second, lumberjacks stuck turning back and forth by their posts for seconds

ljtwitch: the lumberjacks WALKING DOWN THE RAMP in the intro walk steadily: at most one jitter event a lumberjack-second (before the fix: a walker behind another stood a step and walked a step every 8 steps, 2.9 a second; walking back to the post is in the idle check)

ljtwitch: the lumberjacks ON A MAN (the swarm, the roll-in's roller), brawling, leaving the ring, down, in a move or whipped: at most 4 jitter events a lumberjack-second -- hits and moves knock men about, but no walking on the spot, no turning left and right each step (before the fix: 7 to 9 a second, rollers turning between two corners each step, the swarm walking into the apron for seconds)
ljtwitch: the jitter measure ran -- at a match's end, 300 lumberjack-seconds or more idle outside the ring and 20 walking measured

ljround8 / ROUND 9 (at every match's end, over the run so far): the lumberjacks attack the COMPUTER's competitor as much as the player's (the user: 'They attack the player more than the CPU') -- their hits a lumberjack-minute on him, over every match of the run (lj_y), at least 3/4 of the rate on player 1, each with 60 lumberjack-seconds or more, else not judged (ROUND 9: one match's handful of hits was no measure -- r8's lumberjack_twitch5 match 5, the CPU 4 hits in 57 lumberjack-seconds against the player's 21 in 135, the run's whole 7 in 87 against 42 in 484)

ljround8 (at every match's end): the lumberjacks are aggressive -- at least 6 of their hits a minute on a man out there (both competitors together, out 30 s or more in all; ef8edd4: 3.4-7.0, mostly under 6)

ljround8 / ROUND 9 (at every match's end): once a lumberjack holds a man (from the front or from behind, anywhere), the throw in about 60% and the game's own grapple move about 40% (the user) -- the throw 40-80% with 5 holds or more
